## Objective
The objective of this repo is to document the literature search for 
the paper "Artificial intelligence in veterinary diagnostic histopathology".

### Input
- api key (instructions on how to get one are here: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1PwWraSGeOL0qDwtjUIOamBVnPhycoOOdFAnh2b5UxJ0/edit?usp=sharing))

### Issues / deviations / commments
- **ai_dx_bx_vet_v12** selected (see below) - search repeated at 2025-09-09 (same chunk added line)
- The api scopus access relies on UCD access - only works on campus

```{r libraries, directories, and functions, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(bibliometrix)
library (rscopus) #for scopus api
library(tidyverse)
library(jsonlite)
library(writexl)
library(readxl)


to_box <- "~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/"

# Used to extract fields of interest from raw scopus results
extract_fields <- function(entry) {
  tibble(
    scopus_id = entry[["dc:identifier"]],
    title       = entry[["dc:title"]],
    creator     = entry[["dc:creator"]],
    journal     = entry[["prism:publicationName"]],
    coverDate   = entry[["prism:coverDate"]],
    doi         = entry[["prism:doi"]],
    citedby     = entry[["citedby-count"]],
    issn        = entry[["prism:issn"]]
    

  )
}

search_scopus <- function(api_key, search_objective, search_version, database, query) {
  
  # Run the search using provided query and API key
  raw_results <- scopus_search(query, api_key = api_key)

  # Convert results into a structured dataframe
  cleaned_results <- map_dfr(raw_results$entries, extract_fields)
  cleaned_results <- cleaned_results %>%
  mutate(scopus_id = str_replace(`scopus_id`, "SCOPUS_ID:", ""))
  

  # Create metadata dataframe
  metadata <- tibble(
    database = database,
    search_time = Sys.time(),
    objective = search_objective,
    version = search_version,
    query = query,
    n_hits = nrow(cleaned_results)
  )
  

  # Return a list containing all three dataframes
  return(list(
    raw_results = raw_results,
    cleaned_results = cleaned_results,
    metadata = metadata
  ))
}

#Used to retrieve abstracts for samples
get_abstract <- function(id, api_key) {
  Sys.sleep(0.5)  # Pause to avoid hitting rate limits
  result <- tryCatch({
    abstract_retrieval(id, 
                         identifier = "scopus_id", 
                         view = "FULL", 
                         api_key = api_key, 
                         verbose = FALSE)
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Error retrieving abstract for ID ", id, ": ", e$message)
    return(NULL)
  })
  
  if (!is.null(result) && !is.null(result$content)) {
    abstract_text <- result$content$`abstracts-retrieval-response`$coredata$`dc:description`
    if (!is.null(abstract_text)) {
      return(abstract_text)
    } else {
      message("Abstract not found for ID ", id)
    }
  }
  
  return(NA_character_)
}

library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

sample_results <- function(results, sample_size, api_key) {
  
  # Set seed for reproducibility
  set.seed(42)

  # Generate a random sample from the results
  sample <- results[sample(nrow(results), sample_size), ]

  # Retrieve abstracts for the sample using scopus_id
  sample <- sample %>%
    mutate(
      abstract = map_chr(scopus_id, ~ get_abstract(.x, api_key))
    )

  # Create template dataframe with required columns
  template <- sample %>%
    select(scopus_id, title, abstract) %>%
    mutate(tp = "",
           fp_comment = "",
           fp_neg_term_suggestion = "",
           tp_task_term_suggestion = "",
           tp_disease_term_suggestion = "",
           tp_ai_model_term_suggestion = "", 
           tp_other_term_suggestion = ""
    )

  # Return a list with sample and template dataframes
  return(list(
    sample = sample,
    template = template
  ))
}

calculate_search_performance <- function(reviewed_sample, metadata) {
  
  # Calculate performance metrics from the reviewed sample
  sample_n <- nrow(reviewed_sample)
  sample_tp <- sum(reviewed_sample$tp == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
  sample_fp <- sum(reviewed_sample$tp == FALSE, na.rm = TRUE)
  sample_ppv <- sample_tp / (sample_tp + sample_fp)

  # Update metadata dataframe with performance metrics
  performance <- metadata %>%
    mutate(
      sample_n = sample_n,
      sample_tp = sample_tp,
      sample_fp = sample_fp,
      sample_ppv = sample_ppv
    )

  # Return performance dataframe
  return(performance)
}


calculate_search_se_ppv <- function(priors, results, reviewed, metadata) {
  
  #Calculate se based on the priors
  priors_n <- nrow(priors)
  priors_tp <- sum(priors$title %in% results$title)
  priors_fn <-sum(!(priors$title %in% results$title))
  priors_se <- priors_tp / (priors_tp + priors_fn)


  # Calculate ppv from the reviewed sample
  sample_n <- nrow(reviewed)
  sample_tp <- sum(reviewed$tp == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
  sample_fp <- sum(reviewed$tp == FALSE, na.rm = TRUE)
  sample_ppv <- sample_tp / (sample_tp + sample_fp)
  
  

  # Update metadata dataframe with performance metrics
  performance <- metadata %>%
    mutate(
      priors_n = priors_n,
      priors_tp = priors_tp,
      priors_fn = priors_fn,
      priors_se = priors_se,
      sample_n = sample_n,
      sample_tp = sample_tp,
      sample_fp = sample_fp,
      sample_ppv = sample_ppv
    )

  # Return performance dataframe
  return(performance)
}

```


### Search query refinement ai_dx_bx_vet
This section contains documentation for a series of search versions performed to
iteratively update the search query for the search objective.
All search query refinement iterations were done in scopus (using the api interface)

#### Search objective 
Identify records about artificial intelligence applications for veterinary
diagnostic histopathology ("ai_dx_bx_vet")

#### Chunks
Each search version will have a search chunk and most (with some exceptions) will have a performance chunk:
- **scopus_search_ai_dx_bx_vet_<search_version>**
This chunk documents the search, includes a "query rationale" on the reasoning behind the query
and **outputs**:
  - **results_fe_si_dx_bx_vet_<search_version>.json** (artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/lit_search)
  Includes basic search results (title, doi etc) but not abstracts
  - **metadata_fe_si_dx_bx_vet_<search_version>.json** (artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/lit_search)
Includes database, search_time, query and number of hits
  - **sample_fe_si_dx_bx_vet_<search_version>.json** (artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/lit_search)
  For early versions, this is a random sample of size 10 (arbitrary sample size) that in addition to the data from
  results includes the abstract. 
  For later versions (closer to be considered for use) the sample size is set to the full number of hits.
  - **template_fe_si_dx_bx_vet_<search_version>.xlsx** (artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/lit_search)
  This is a template based on the sample, but parsed to be used for manual review.
- **search_performance_ai_dx_bx_vet_<search_version>**.
This chunk tests the search performance by 
1) comparing the results to a set of preidentified records of interest to assess search sensitivity
2) Manually assessing the sample (sample_fe_si_dx_bx_vet_<search_version>.json) to assess search ppv
Each search performance chunk takes the input:
  - **ai_dx_bx_vet_prior.xlsx** (input/) or **ai_dx_bx_vet_priors_<search_version>**
  spreadsheet with preidentified papers I know are of interest (to calculate sensitivity. 
  Updated with each sample to extend the list of TP (disqualifies direct comparisons of se between searches)
  - **reviewed_ai_dx_bx_vet_v1.xlsx** (input/reviewed_lit_search)
  Manually reviewed sample from the search (using template_fe_si_dx_bx_vet_<search_version>.xlsx)
  - **results_fe_si_dx_bx_vet_<search_version>.json** (artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/lit_search)
  - **metadata_fe_si_dx_bx_vet_<search_version>.json** (artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/lit_search)
Each search_performance chunk outputs:
  - **performance_ai_dx_bx_vet_<search_version>.json** (artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/lit_search)
  sensitivity and ppv
  - **priors_v<search_version+1>.json** (artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/priors/)
  An updated list of tp, based on the initial priors and tp identified in earlier samples (this strategy makes the sensitivity estimate more reliable for later search versions, but disqualifies direct comparison of sensitivity between searches)
  - **parsed_reviewed_ai_dx_bx_vet_<search_version>.json** (artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/lit_search)
  Only for "late" versions - with parsed exclusion reasons for assessment)
  - **exclusion_<search_version>.png** (artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/lit_search) breakdown of exclusion
  Only for "late" versions - figure with exclusion reasons for assessment)
  
#### Query selection
Based on evaluation of the search versions in scopus, the query in 
**ai_dx_bx_vet_v12** was selected for the study. This query prioritized sensitivity (100%), over ppv (29%), opting against negative (AND NOT) type search terms (apart from Abstract titles). 
The runner up query was version 13, including negative search terms for the other modalites than histopathology (by far the largest group of FP). This version had a sensitivity of 97% and a ppv of 49%. 

#####  scopus_search_ai_dx_bx_vet_v1
This is the first version (v1) of a search for articles on artificial intelligence applications
for veterinary diagnostic pathology (ai_dx_bx_vet).
This query was designed to cast a wide net (be sensitive) for articles on artificial intelligence
applications for veterinary diagnostic pathology. 
The initial query was designed to capture a list of articles we were familiar with and that fit the
scope. Listed here:
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1NQ1F3EcLAciNyOxIDa67xlyQqWmXD7GOZaMlJk6fp4A/edit?usp=sharing

```{r scopus_search_ai_dx_bx_vet_v1}
api_key <- readLines(paste0(to_box, "judits_work_keller_labs/fe_si_papers/artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/input/elsevier_api_key.txt"))

search_objective <- "ai_dx_bx_vet"
search_version <- "v1"
database = "scopus"

query <- 'TITLE-ABS-KEY ( ( "artificial intelligence" OR "machine learning*" OR "deep learning*") AND ( "patholog*" OR "biops*" OR "histolog*" or "histopatholog*" ) AND ( "canine"  OR "feline" OR "equine" OR "veterinar*")) AND ( LIMIT-TO ( DOCTYPE , "ar" ) ) AND ( LIMIT-TO ( LANGUAGE , "English" ) )'

output_dir <- "~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_labs/fe_si_papers/artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/lit_search/"

ai_dx_bx_vet_v1 <- search_scopus(api_key, search_objective, search_version, database, query)

results <-  ai_dx_bx_vet_v1$cleaned_results
metadata <- ai_dx_bx_vet_v1$metadata

write_json(results, paste0(output_dir, "results_", search_objective, "_", search_version, ".json"))
write_json(metadata, paste0(output_dir, "metadata_", search_objective, "_", search_version, ".json"))


#Sample 10 search hits and prepare a template for manual review
sample_size <- 10

sample_ai_dx_bx_human_v1 <- sample_results(results, sample_size, api_key)

sample <- sample_ai_dx_bx_vet_v1$sample 
template <- sample_ai_dx_bx_vet_v1$template %>%
  filter(!(is.na(abstract)))

write_json(sample, paste0(output_dir, "sample_", search_objective, "_", search_version, ".json"))
write_xlsx(template, paste0(output_dir, "template_", search_objective, "_", search_version, ".xlsx"))
```
#####  search_performance_ai_dx_bx_vet_v1
100% sensitivity nut only 22% ppv.
False positives consisted of 
- One experimental (non diagnostic) in monkeys - consider adding common lab species as negative terms
- Two reviews (one would be removed by adding neg term "review", the other by not using "veterinar*" (could instead specify species of interest - would also eliminate lab animal problem))
- One cell culture study using "Madin-Darby Canine Kidney Cells"; "MDCK"
- One about a veterinary anatomy tutoring system (mentions histology which I want to keep, consider skipping "veterinar*)
- Two about other modalities (but using histopath for validation) - one "MRI", one "optical coherence tomography"
```{r, search_performance_ai_dx_bx_vet_v1}

input_dir <- paste0(to_box, "judits_work_keller_labs/fe_si_papers/artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/input/")
reviewed_dir <- paste0(to_box, "judits_work_keller_labs/fe_si_papers/artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/input/reviewed_lit_search/")
output_dir <- paste0(to_box, "judits_work_keller_labs/fe_si_papers/artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/lit_search/")
priors_dir <- paste0(to_box, "judits_work_keller_labs/fe_si_papers/artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/priors/")


search_objective <- "ai_dx_bx_vet"
search_version <- "v1"

priors <- read_xlsx(paste0(input_dir, "ai_dx_bx_vet_priors_v1.xlsx"))

results <- fromJSON(paste0(output_dir, "results_", search_objective, "_", search_version, ".json"))
reviewed <- read_xlsx(paste0(reviewed_dir, "reviewed_", search_objective, "_", search_version, ".xlsx"))
metadata <- fromJSON(paste0(output_dir, "metadata_", search_objective, "_", search_version, ".json"))

write_json(priors, paste0(priors_dir, "priors_v1.json"))

add_to_priors <- reviewed %>% 
  filter(tp) %>% 
  filter (!title %in% priors$title) %>%
  select(scopus_id, title, abstract)

priors <- bind_rows(priors, add_to_priors)


performance <- calculate_search_se_ppv(priors, results, reviewed, metadata)
write_json(performance, paste0(output_dir, "performance_", search_objective, "_", search_version, ".json"))
write_json(priors, paste0(priors_dir, "priors_v2.json" ))
```

- removing "veterinar*"

##### search_performance_ai_dx_bx_vet_v2
Se 92.8%, ppv 50%
- One unexpected "FN" record was eliminated when using "tomography" as negativ term (even though did not contain the word)
FPs were:
- One paper using cats as experimental species (could try negative searcg term "feline model" although that would risk potentially decreasing sensivity)
- One editorial (try neg term "editorial")
- One gait analysis paper - reconsider "patholog*" since the term is so wide - maybe add "image"
- One risk prediction paper same comment as above -reconsider Pathol* or add image*
- One on "biodynamic imaging" - try using "biodynamic" as negative term

##### scopus_search_ai_dx_bx_vet_v12
Based on assessments of versions v8-v10 (where negative search terms "AND NOT" were iteratively removed),
and the consideration to prioritize sensitivity over ppv for this search (since number of records is
managable even with a more inclusive approach), the query for this version removed negative search terms and added 
the positive search term "veterinar*" to capture possible non feline, canine or equine records. 

```{r, scopus_search_ai_dx_bx_vet_v12}
api_key <- readLines("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/input/elsevier_api_key.txt")

search_version <- "v12"

output_dir <- "~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/lit_search/"

results <-  results_and_metadata$cleaned_results
metadata <- results_and_metadata$metadata

write_json(results, paste0(output_dir, "results_", search_objective, "_", search_version, "_", Sys.Date(), ".json"))
write_json(metadata, paste0(output_dir, "metadata_", search_objective, "_", search_version, "_", Sys.Date(),".json"))

#Get abstracts and prep template for the full search (set sample size to full list to use same function)
#sample_size <- 120
sample_size <- 138

sample_and_template <- sample_results(results, sample_size, api_key)
```

##### scopus_search_ai_dx_bx_vet_v13
Most FP in v12 were not histopathology studies. For a veterinary search the total number
of records are still managable, but if we later would like to use a similar query for 
human ai for histopathology papers, we may want to prioritize ppv. This query explores 
excluding some records in a vet search (to make it comparable with a similar human search)

```{r, scopus_search_ai_dx_bx_vet_v13}
api_key <- readLines(paste0(to_box, "judits_work_keller_labs/fe_si_papers/artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/input/elsevier_api_key.txt"))

search_objective <- "ai_dx_bx_vet"
search_version <- "v13"
database = "scopus"

query <- 'TITLE-ABS-KEY ( ( "artificial intelligence" OR "machine learning*" OR "deep learning*") AND ( "patholog*" OR "biops*" OR "histolog*" or "histopatholog*" ) AND ("image*" OR "computer vision") AND ( "canine"  OR "feline" OR "equine" OR "veterinar*") AND NOT ("MR*" OR "Magnetic resonance*" OR "radiograph*" OR "computed tomography" OR "ultrasound" OR "cytology" OR "cytopathology" OR "optical coherence tomography")) AND NOT (TITLE("Abstract:"))  AND ( LIMIT-TO ( LANGUAGE , "English" ) ) AND ( LIMIT-TO ( DOCTYPE , "ar" ) OR LIMIT-TO ( DOCTYPE , "cp" ) )'

output_dir <- "~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_labs/fe_si_papers/artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/lit_search/"

results_and_metadata <- search_scopus(api_key, search_objective, search_version, database, query)

results <-  results_and_metadata$cleaned_results
metadata <- results_and_metadata$metadata

write_json(results, paste0(output_dir, "results_", search_objective, "_", search_version, ".json"))
write_json(metadata, paste0(output_dir, "metadata_", search_objective, "_", search_version, ".json"))
```

##### search_performance_ai_dx_bx_vet_v13
Since this only adds negative keywords compared with v12,no new hits are expected.
This chunks confirms that, and used the reviewed v12 to see if the added negative terms 
resulted in loss of TPs or FPs. 
Only one histopathology study was lost by adding the negative keywords for other modalities,
this was a book chapter and although with an (improper) keyword "cytology" for a histopathology study.
Considered worth keeping the negative keywords for the improved performance

```{r, search_performance_ai_dx_bx_vet_v13}
#none as expected
in_v13_not_in_v12 <- results %>% filter(!(scopus_id %in% results_v12$scopus_id))
```

### pubmed_searches
Searches in pubmed were perfomed based on the selected query ai_bx_dx_vet_v12, and the runner-up ai_bx_dx_vet_v13 (less sensitive)
The pubmed searches were performed on the web interface on 2025-03-27 (for version 12) and 2025-03-24 (for version 13).
The queries were adjusted to account for the search format on pubmed (title, abstract and MESH terms searched separately, keywords adjusted to fit MESH terms). 
Each pubmed search are documented in chunks below
- **pubmed_ai_dx_bx_vet_<search_version>**
Each with the input files
  - **query_ai_dx_bx_vet_<search_version>_pubmed.txt** (artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/pub_med/)
  Containing the copy-pasted pubmed query
  - **ai_dx_bx_vet_<search_version>_pubmed.csv** (artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/pub_med/)
  Downloaed pubmed results
  - **results_ai_dx_bx_vet_<search_version>.json** (/artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/lit_search/)
  Downloaded scopus results
  - **parsed_reviewed_ai_dx_bx_<search_version>.json** (/artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/lit_search/)
  Parsed reviewed scopus results (parsed exclusion reason)
  - **reviewed_pubmed_new_ai_dx_bx_vet_<search_version>.xlsx**
  Manually reveiwed new records (based on template output in same chunk)
And output: 
  - **template_pubmed_new_ai_dx_bx_vet_<search_version>.xlsx** (/artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/lit_search/)
  - **exclusion_vet_<search_version>_scopus_and_pubmed.png** (/artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/lit_search/)
  Figure with exclusions
  - **lit_search_for_flowchart_vet_<search_version>.xlsx** (/artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/lit_search/)
  - **summary_<search_version>.xlsx** (/artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/lit_search/)
  - **template_articles_ai_dx_bx_vet_<search_version>.xlsx** (/artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/lit_search/)
  Template for full article review - only for v12

```{r, pubmed_ai_dx_bx_vet_v12}
excluded_not_bx <- nrow(not_histopathology)

excluded_not_diagnostic <- nrow(not_dx)
excluded_not_veterinary <- nrow(not_veterinary)
sought_for_retreival <- nrow(retreive)
```

```{r, pubmed_ai_dx_bx_vet_v13}
  records_identified = records_identified,
  records_id_scopus = records_identified_from_scopus,
  records_id_pubmed = records_identified_from_pubmed,
  records_removed_before_screening = records_without_abstract + duplicates_records_removed,
  records_wo_abstracts = records_without_abstract,
  duplicates_records_removed = duplicates_records_removed,
  records_screened = records_screened,
  screened_records_excluded = screened_records_excluded_n,
  excluded_not_research = excluded_not_research,
  excluded_not_diagnostic = excluded_not_diagnostic,
  excluded_not_veterinary = excluded_not_veterinary,
  excluded_not_histopathology = excluded_not_bx,
  sought_for_retreival = sought_for_retreival
  
  
)



p <- v13_reviewed %>%
  count(tp, exclusion) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = tp, y = n, fill = exclusion)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(x = "Relevant search hit", y = "Count", fill = "Exclusion Reason") +
  theme_bw()

print(p)

ggsave(paste0(output_dir, "exclusion_vet_v13_scopus_and_pubmed.png"),
       plot = p,
       dpi = 300,
       width = 90,
       height = 90,
       units = "mm")

summary_vet_v13_scopus_and_pubmed <- v13_reviewed %>%
  summarise(
    total_records = n(),
    total_tp_true = sum(tp == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  bind_cols(
    reviewed_v13 %>% count(exclusion) %>% tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = exclusion, values_from = n)
  )

write_xlsx(lit_search_for_flowchart, paste0(output_dir, "lit_search_for_flowchart_vet_v13.xlsx"))
write_xlsx(summary_vet_v13_scopus_and_pubmed,paste0(output_dir, "summary_v13.xlsx") )
```

### Scopus search ai_dx_bx_human_v1
This is the first version (v1) of a search for articles on artificial intelligence
applications for human diagnostic pathology (ai_dx_bx_human)

#### Query rationale
This query was designed based to case a wide net for AI for histopathology (in english,
with document type limited to article (excludes reviews, editorials, letters and conference papers)).

#### Input
- api_key directory

#### Output
- results_ai_dx_bx_humans_v1.json (output/lit_search) (with all search results)
- metadata_ai_dx_bx_humans_v1.json (output/lit_search) (with search metadata)
- sample_ai_dx_bx_humans_v1.json (output/lit_search) (sample for review)
- template_ai_dx_bx_humans_v1.json (output/lit_search) (template for manual review of sample)

```{r, search ai_dx_bx_human_v1,  warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

api_key <- readLines(paste0(to_box, "judits_work_keller_labs/fe_si_papers/artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/input/elsevier_api_key.txt"))

search_objective <- "ai_dx_bx_human"
search_version <- "v1"
database = "scopus"

query <- 'TITLE-ABS-KEY ( ( "artificial intelligence" OR "AI" OR "machine learning" OR "deep learning" OR "computer vision" OR "neural network*" OR "computational" ) W/3 ( "pathology" OR "biopsy" ) AND ( "human" ) ) AND ( LIMIT-TO ( DOCTYPE , "ar" ) ) AND ( LIMIT-TO ( LANGUAGE , "English" ) )'

output_dir <- "~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_labs/fe_si_papers/artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/output/lit_search/"

ai_dx_bx_human_v1 <- search_scopus(api_key, search_objective, search_version, database, query)

results <-  ai_dx_bx_human_v1$cleaned_results
metadata <- ai_dx_bx_human_v1$metadata

write_json(results, paste0(output_dir, "results_", search_objective, "_", search_version, ".json"))
write_json(metadata, paste0(output_dir, "metadata_", search_objective, "_", search_version, ".json"))


#Sample 10 search hits and prepare a template for manual review
sample_size <- 10

sample_ai_dx_bx_human_v1 <- sample_results(results, sample_size, api_key)

sample <- sample_ai_dx_bx_human_v1$sample
template <- sample_ai_dx_bx_human_v1$template

write_json(sample, paste0(output_dir, "sample_", search_objective, "_", search_version, ".json"))
write_xlsx(template, paste0(output_dir, "template_", search_objective, "_", search_version, ".xlsx"))

```

### Search performance ai_dx_bx_human_v1
Calculates the ppv for ai_dx_bx_human_v1 (used to draft query for v2)

#### Input
- reviewed_ai_dx_bx_humans_v1.xlsx (input/reviewed_lit_search)
This consists of a manually reviewed sample from the search

#### Output
- performance_ai_dx_bx_humans_v1.json (output/lit_search)

#### Assessment
This version of the search had a ppv of 20%. 
- Four false positive were reviews (would be eliminated by adding the negative search term "review")
- One was a perspective paper (would be eliminated by adding the negative search term "perspective paper")
- Two were on cytopathology (not histopathology") one of them als oa review - consider adding negative search term "cytopathology"
- One was on cytogenetics and karyotypes (Don't expect this to be a large category but consider adding negative term "karyotype")
- One was a suggested framework for data annotation (I have no good negative search terms for this, adding "framework" would risk eliminating too many TPs)




### Search performance ai_dx_bx_human_v2
Calculates the ppv for ai_dx_bx_human_v2 (used to draft query for v3)

#### Input
- reviewed_ai_dx_bx_humans_v2.xlsx (input/reviewed_lit_search)
This consists of a manually reviewed sample from the search

#### Output
- performance_ai_dx_bx_humans_v2.json (output/lit_search) 

#### Assessment
This version of the search had a ppv of 30%
False postives were:
- Two veterinary papers (one canine on liquid biopsies and one equine on cytology - suggested neg terms "canine" "liquid biopsy", "equine", "cytology" consider adding "feline", "murine", "mice", "rats" and "veterinary" as negative terms)
- Two on AI for other modalities (one on ultrasound and one on optic coherence tomography) - consider adding negative search terms "ultrasound" and "tomography"
- One was conferece proceedings (consider adding neg term "proceedings")
- One was on "activity index" abbreviated as "AI" consider removing "AI" as search term and see how many fewer hits or adding "acitvity index" as negative term
- One used a language model to parse info from pathology reports (considered negative term "language model" bt that risks
eliminating vision-language models so maybe better to accept this)

### Scopus search ai_dx_bx_human_v3

#### Query rationale
based on "v2" but removed "AI" to avoid other abbreviations (such as acitvity index)
#### Input
- api_key directory

#### Output
- results_ai_dx_bx_humans_v3.json (output/lit_search)  (with all search results)
- metadata_ai_dx_bx_humans_v3.json (output/lit_search)  (with search metadata)
- sample_ai_dx_bx_humans_diff_v2_v3.json (output/lit_search)  (sample for review)
- template_ai_dx_bx_humans_diff_v2_v3.json (output/lit_search) (template for manual review of sample)

#### Comment
This is a little different from previous assessments since it evaluates the search hits lost by removing the term "AI".
Removing "AI" as search term resulted in 160 less hits. A sample of hits that occured in v2 but not v3, revealed that 
50% (5/10) were TP and 50% were FP. Of the FP one was a FP for another reason "liquid biopsy" and four becasue
AI stood for something else "activity index", apoptotic index", "apoptosis index" or "aortic insufficency".
Surprisingly many of the TP in this did mention other search terms like "Artificial intelligence" and "Deep Learning".
Consider explicitly making the search case insensitive.

```{r, search ai_dx_bx_human_v3,  warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
metadata <- ai_dx_bx_human_v3$metadata

write_json(results, paste0(output_dir, "results_", search_objective, "_", search_version, ".json"))
write_json(metadata, paste0(output_dir, "metadata_", search_objective, "_", search_version, ".json"))

results_v3 <- fromJSON(paste0(output_dir, "results_ai_dx_bx_human_v3.json"))
```

### Search performance ai_dx_bx_human_v7
Calculates the ppv for ai_dx_bx_human_v7 (used to draft query for v7)

#### Assessment
This version of the search had a ppv of 67%

```{r}
new_pubmed_2025_sept <- read_csv("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/pub_med/ai_dx_bx_vet_v12_pubmed_2025-09-09.csv")

duplicates <- new_pubmed_2025_sept %>% filter(DOI %in% new_scopus_2025_sept$doi)

new_pubmed_not_duplicate <- new_pubmed_2025_sept %>% filter(!DOI %in% new_scopus_2025_sept$doi)

### Read in previously reviewed records
parsed_reviewed_scopus_2025_march <- fromJSON(paste0(output_dir, "parsed_reviewed_ai_dx_bx_v12.json")) 

#Create template based on parsed previously reviewed scopus search
template_new <- parsed_reviewed_scopus_2025_march %>%
  rename(database_id = scopus_id,
         title = title,
         first_author = creator,
         date = coverDate) %>%
  mutate(database = "scopus") %>%
  select(database_id, database, title, first_author,date, doi, abstract, tp, fp_comment, exclusion)

#Filter scopus records to add
add_scopus_to_template <- new_scopus_2025_sept %>%
  filter(!doi %in% template_new$doi) %>%
  rename(database_id = scopus_id,
         title = title,
         first_author = creator,
         date = coverDate) %>%
  mutate(database = "scopus",
         tp = "",
         fp_comment = "",
         exclusion = "") %>%
  select(database_id, database, title, first_author, date, doi, abstract, tp, fp_comment, exclusion)

template_new_scopus_added <- rbind(template_new, add_scopus_to_template)

add_pubmed_to_template <- new_pubmed_2025_sept %>%
  filter(!DOI %in% template_new_scopus_added$doi) %>%
  mutate(database = "scopus",
         abstract = "fetch",
         tp = "",
         fp_comment = "",
         exclusion = "") %>%
  rename(database_id = PMID,
         title = Title,
         first_author = `First Author`,
         date = `Create Date`,
         doi = DOI
         ) %>%
  select(database_id, database, title, first_author, date, doi, abstract, tp, fp_comment, exclusion)

template_full <- rbind(template_new_scopus_added, add_pubmed_to_template)

missing_abstract <- template_full %>% filter(is.na(abstract))

template <- template_full %>% filter(!is.na(abstract))

write_xlsx(template, paste0(output_dir, "records_for_screening_2025-09-09.xlsx"))

screened_records <- read_xlsx("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation/input/screened_records/screened_records_2025-09-09.xlsx")

records_excluded <- screened_records %>% filter(tp == FALSE)

not_biopsy <- records_excluded %>% filter(exclusion == "not_biopsy")
not_research_paper <- records_excluded %>% filter(exclusion == "not_research_paper")
not_diagnostic <- records_excluded %>% filter(exclusion == "not_diagnostic")
not_veterinary <- records_excluded %>% filter(exclusion == "not_veterinary")
sought_for_retreival <- screened_records %>% filter(tp == TRUE)
```
